chunks.arabic_text: ١٧ - مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ، الْبَرْقِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، مَوْلَى جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ.

translations.en: 17 – Muhammad ibn Khalid, al-Barqi, son of Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, Abu Abdillah, client of Jarir ibn Abdillah.

chunks.arabic_text: حَدِيثُهُ يُعْرَفُ وَيُنْكَرُ. يَرْوِي عَنِ الضُّعَفَاءِ كَثِيرًا وَيَعْتَمِدُ الْمَرَاسِيلَ.

translations.en: His hadith are recognized and denied. He narrates a lot from the weak (narrators) and relies on the mursal traditions.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Ḍuʿafāʾ* characterizes Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī as a figure of mixed reliability, whose narrations are simultaneously recognized and disputed by scholars. The critique specifically targets his frequent reliance on weak transmitters and his use of *mursal* (disconnected) chains, reflecting the rigorous scrutiny applied to early hadith compilers in Shia scholarship. This assessment underscores the importance of chain integrity (*isnād*) in validating theological and legal traditions.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi's hadith narrations?
